- **Strengths:** Reduces global memory atomic contention for spatially clustered points by aggregating them in shared memory first [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly describes a CUDA kernel implementation that uses a block-level shared memory cache for aggregating 3D points. It details the logic where threads first attempt to claim a slot in shared memory using `atomicCAS`. If successful, they perform reductions (sums) in shared memory. If a collision occurs (the slot is occupied), the kernel falls back to performing atomic operations on global memory (`d_grid`). This mechanism directly supports the claim that the method reduces global memory atomic contention by aggregating points in shared memory first, only resorting to global memory atomics when necessary (cache collisions).
